get.description:
Searches for and returns pages of dashboards using a variety of filters. Search is eventually-consistent; changes to dashboards may take a few seconds to reflect in search results.

Also supports retrieving pages of archived dashboards; however, the following restrictions apply: only the `limit` and `after` parameters are respected, all others are ignored; archived dashboard retrieval does not support filtering, custom sorting, or property projection. Results are always returned in order from most recently deleted to least recently deleted.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: A cursor token for pagination. Use the value from the previous response's paging.next.after field.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: Whether to retrieve archived dashboards only. Default false.

parameters.name: businessUnitIds
parameters.description: Filter to dashboards that are a part of the specified business units.

parameters.name: createdAfter
parameters.description: Filter to dashboards created after the specified date and time.

parameters.name: createdBefore
parameters.description: Filter to dashboards created before the specified date and time.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: Filter to dashboards with the specified IDs.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of results to display per page. Default 25, max 100.

parameters.name: onlyFavorites
parameters.description: Filter to only dashboards that are favorited by the requesting user. Default false.

parameters.name: ownerUserIds
parameters.description: Filter to dashboards owned by the specified users.

parameters.name: properties
parameters.description: Additionally properties to include in the response. Refer to the response details for available fields.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Filter to dashboards whose name or description contains the search string.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort field and direction. Supported fields are `name`, `updatedAt`, and `lastViewedAt`. Defaults to `-updatedAt`

parameters.name: tagIds
parameters.description: Filter to dashboards tagged with the specified tags.

parameters.name: updatedAfter
parameters.description: Filter to dashboards updated after the specified date and time.

parameters.name: updatedBefore
parameters.description: Filter to dashboards updated before the specified date and time.

post.description:
Creates a new dashboard. Existing reports can optionally be attached to the dashboard at creation time; report widgets will be appended sequentially.

Attaching reports to the dashboard is done on a best-effort basis, and it's possible that some or all reports may fail to be attached. The dashboard will still be created, and no error will be returned. The requestor should check the `widgets` field in the response object to see which reports were successfully attached.

Archives one or more dashboards. Already-archived dashboards are silently ignored. The maximum batch size is 500.

If any of the requested items fail, the response code will be `207 Multi-Status` and the response will include details of individual failures.

Archived dashboards are purged after 90 days.

Restores one or more archived dashboards. Already-active dashboards are silently ignored. The maximum batch size is 500.

If any of the requested items fail, the response code will be `207 Multi-Status` and the response will include details of individual failures.

Updates the owner of one or more dashboards. The maximum batch size is 500.

If any of the requested items fail, the response code will be `207 Multi-Status` and the response will include details of individual failures.

Updates the permissions for one or more dashboards. The maximum batch size is 500.

If any of the requested items fail, the response code will be `207 Multi-Status` and the response will include details of individual failures.

get.description:
Retrieves a single dashboard.

Also supports retrieving archived dashboards via the `archived` query parameter. Retrieving archived dashboards requires the requesting user to be the dashboard owner, a reporting admin, or a super admin.

parameters.name: dashboardId
parameters.description: The ID of the dashboard to retrieve.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: Whether to retrieve an archived dashboard instead of an active one. Default false.

parameters.name: properties
parameters.description: Additionally properties to include in the response. Refer to the response details for available fields.

patch.description:
Partially updates a dashboard. All fields in the request are optional; only the fields which are present will be updated.

Can also be used to archive or restore a dashboard using the `archived` field. When `archived` is present in a request, it must be the only field present, or it will result in an error. Archived dashboards are purged after 90 days.

parameters.name: dashboardId
parameters.description: The ID of the dashboard to update.

post.description:
Adds one or more reports to a dashboard. Report widgets are appended to the end of the existing dashboard layout. Any reports which are already on the dashboard, don't exist, or the requesting user doesn't have permissions for are skipped. Check the dashboard in the response to determine which reports were successfully added.

Dashboards cannot have more than 50 reports on them; attempting to add beyond that limit will fail.

parameters.name: dashboardId
parameters.description: The ID of the dashboard to add reports to.

post.description: Clones an existing dashboard. The cloned dashboard may either retain references to the reports on the original dashboard, or clone the original's reports and reference the clones.

parameters.name: dashboardId
parameters.description: The ID of the dashboard to clone.

post.description:
Exports a dashboard's content to one or more HubSpot users via standard HubSpot communication channels (notably, email).

Status tracking is not available; a successful request will result in a `204 No Content` response.

Any set of HubSpot users can be specified as the recipients. However, if a given user does not have access to reporting, does not have CRM export permissions, etc., then they will receive a notification with an error rather than a successful export.

**NOTE: This API can only be called from apps with user-level access.** Attempting to call from an app with account-level access (including legacy apps) will fail, because only real users can request exports.

parameters.name: dashboardId
parameters.description: The ID of the dashboard to export.

put.description:
Adds a single report to a dashboard. The report widget is appended to the end of the existing dashboard layout. If the report is already on the dashboard, does not exist, or the requesting user doesn't have permission to access it, does nothing. Check the dashboard in the response to determine whether the report was successfully added.

Dashboards cannot have more than 50 reports on them; attempting to add beyond that limit will fail.

parameters.name: dashboardId
parameters.description: The ID of the dashboard to modify

parameters.name: reportId
parameters.description: The ID of the report to add to the dashboard.

delete.description: Removes a single report from a dashboard.

parameters.name: dashboardId
parameters.description: The ID of the dashboard to modify.

parameters.name: reportId
parameters.description: The ID of the report to remove from the dashboard.

exportType.description:
The type of export to perform. Valid values are:
- `SCREENSHOT`: Individual report screenshots.
- `PDF`: PDF with individual report screenshots.
- `PPTX` PPTX with individual report screenshots.
- `ZIP`: ZIP of individual report screenshots.
- `CSV`: ZIP with one or more CSV files per report.
- `XLS`: ZIP with one or more XLS files per report.
- `XLSX: ZIP with one or more XLSX files per report.

message.description: The message to include with the export. Optional, empty by default.

recipientUserIds.description: Array of user IDs to send the export to. If absent or empty, the requesting user is used as the sole recipient; otherwise, this exact set of users is used.

subject.description: The subject line to use for the export. If absent, the name of the requested report will be used. Max length of 100 characters.

permissionType.description:
The type of permission to apply to the report. Valid values are:
- PRIVATE: The report is only accessible to its owner and administrators.
- EVERYONE_VIEW: The report is viewable by everyone.
- EVERYONE_EDIT: The report is viewable and editable by everyone.
- SPECIFIC: In addition to the owner, specific users and/or teams are granted VIEW or EDIT permissions. The `specificPermissions` field must also be present.

specificPermissions.description:
Array of specific permission grants. Must be present when `permissionType` is set to `SPECIFIC`, ignored otherwise.

Dashboards can have one or two specific permission configurations: one for VIEW grants and/or one for EDIT grants. Specific users and/or teams receive either VIEW or EDIT permissions based on which configuration they appear in. A given user or team cannot appear in both VIEW and EDIT configurations.
